Build the UI described below as a single page in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Once UI (`@once-ui-system/core` 2.1) is installed and its standard providers are mounted in the root layout; its agent documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/AGENTS.md`).

Task: Settings page — sidebar sections, profile form (avatar upload, inputs, selects), danger zone.

Requirements:
- Write exactly one file, `app/page.tsx`, that default-exports the page. Put "use client" at the top if the page uses state, effects or event handlers.
- Do not create or change any other file. The root layout, global styles and the stack's standard providers already exist. You can read the project's existing files under `project/`.
- Use realistic placeholder content defined inline in the file (no lorem ipsum). Load nothing from the network: no external image, font or API URLs.
- The page must type-check under strict TypeScript, pass `next build`, and render without console errors.
- Make it responsive from phone to desktop, and accessible.
- Reply with the complete file in a single ```tsx code block and nothing else.

# Once UI — compact codegen rules Load with the task's bundle, `@once-ui-system/core/ai/bundles/{intent}.json`: one file with the task, every component slice it names, their types and its gotchas. For an app shell, a sidebar nav or an editor, read `ai/layouts.md` first — those are the shapes that are hard to get right from props alone. For production-quality composition, read matching Pro blocks from `examples/blocks/manifest.json`. Fetch a slice from `components/` only for a component the bundle does not have. Read everything you need in one step, before writing: every file you read is sent again on every later turn, so a dozen small reads cost far more than one or two large ones. Never hex/rgb — inline SVG `fill`/`stroke` included: `currentColor` or `var(--brand-solid-strong)`. - `background` also: `surface | overlay | page | transparent` ## Typography - Hero: `display-strong-l` or `display-strong-xl` - Section titles: `display-strong-xs` or `display-strong-s` — not `heading-*` - Eyebrow: `` - Text on layout: `textVariant` + `onBackground` on Row/Column instead of nesting Text ## Decoration Absolute layers always: `position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fill pointerEvents="none"`, content `zIndex={1}`. - `zIndex` only inside that layer group (or on a sticky header over its pane). Never on a lone element, never a page-wide ladder. - Gradient `width`: quarter-percent (400 = 100%). Glows: 100–200. - Glow colors: `brand-alpha-medium`, not `brand-background-weak` - Ambient layers on full-bleed section wrapper, outside `maxWidth` column - Budget: one ambient layer per section; motion in hero + one CTA max ## Motion - `RevealFx delay` (and `ShineFx`/`CountFx`/`TypeFx speed`) in **milliseconds**: `delay={index * 100}` — `* 0.1` was 1.8.x. `speed` on `MatrixFx`, `WeatherFx`, `ParticleFx` is a multiplier - `RevealFx translateY`: number = rem; prefer `"8"`–`"16"` tokens - Viewport-reveal with `useInViewport` + latch into `RevealFx revealed`; `CountFx` driven by `value`, no trigger prop - Animate all siblings in a set or none — never one lone animated card ## Components | Need | Use | |------|-----| | Image | `Media` | | Link | `SmartLink` / `Button href` | | Status dot | `StatusIndicator` | | Loading | `Spinner` / `Skeleton` | | Scroll fade | `Fade` as edge strip, not wrapper | | Icons | `IconName`, from `iconNames` in `catalog.json` only | | Logos grid | `LogoCloud` with `columns` set | | Tabs | `Tabs` > `TabList` > `Tab`, `TabPanel` (`orientation="vertical"` for a settings nav) | | Mobile nav, side sheet | `Drawer`, not a hand-made overlay | | Page trail | `Breadcrumbs items={[...]}` | | Keyboard shortcut | `useHotkeys("mod+k", fn)` + `KeyTip keys="mod+k"` | | Screen-reader text, skip link | `VisuallyHidden` | | MDX content | `mdxComponents` / `createMdxComponents` from `/mdx` | ## Imports Most things come from the package root. # Once UI — application layouts

Recipes for the shells a product sits inside, as opposed to the decoration in
`recipes.md`. Each is the shape a working product converged on, not a sketch.

Use them verbatim, then adjust. The values that look arbitrary usually are not —
the notes say which ones matter and why.

All three compile: they are also `ai/examples/app-shell.tsx`, which `pnpm
typecheck` covers, so a renamed prop breaks the recipe rather than leaving it
quietly wrong.

## 1. App shell with a sidebar

The one agents get wrong most often. A dashboard built without this scrolls the
whole document, so the header and sidebar slide away and the nav has to be
scrolled back to.

```tsx
// The drawer is open for the path it was opened on: a link in it closes it.
const [menuPath, setMenuPath] = useState<string | null>(null);
const menuOpen = menuPath === pathname;

<Column fill horizontal="center" flex={1}>
  <Row height="56" fillWidth vertical="center" paddingX="16" gap="8">  {/* 56px: --header-height */}
    <Row hide s={{ hide: false }}>
      <IconButton icon="moreHorizontal" variant="tertiary" tooltip="Menu"
        aria-expanded={menuOpen} onClick={() => setMenuPath(pathname)} />
    </Row>
    {/* logo, search, account */}
  </Row>
  <Row fill paddingX="8">
    <Column s={{ hide: true }} maxWidth={18} fitHeight position="sticky" top="56">
      <Nav nav={nav} pathname={pathname} />
    </Column>
    <Row fill horizontal="center" topRadius="l" overflow="hidden">
      <Row
        height="below-header"
        overflowY="auto"
        topRadius="l"
        horizontal="center"
        fillWidth
        background="surface">
        <Column maxWidth="xl" gap="m" paddingY="32" fitHeight>
          {children}
        </Column>
      </Row>
    </Row>
  </Row>
  <Drawer open={menuOpen} onClose={() => setMenuPath(null)} side="left" size="s" title="Menu" flush>
    <Column paddingTop="64" paddingBottom="16">
      <Nav nav={nav} pathname={pathname} />
    </Column>
  </Drawer>
</Column>
```

What each part is doing:

- **The pane scrolls, not the page.** `height="below-header"` plus
  `overflowY="auto"` is what keeps the header and sidebar in place. It is
  `calc(100dvh - var(--header-height))`, written once as a utility class:
  `dvh`, not `vh` — on mobile `vh` ignores the browser chrome and the pane runs
  off-screen. Never restate the header height in a `calc()` of your own.
- **`--header-height`** is 56px (`var(--static-space-56)`) by default, the
  header this recipe uses. A shell with a different header sets it once on
  `:root`; `height`, `minHeight` and `maxHeight` all take `"below-header"`,
  and a mobile menu hanging from the header takes `maxHeight="below-header"`.
- **`position="sticky" top="56"`** on the sidebar, matching the header height
  (`top="calc(var(--header-height))"` follows a non-default one). `fitHeight`
  so it does not stretch and fight the sticky.
- **`topRadius="l"` + `background="surface"`** is what makes the content read as
  a panel sitting on the page rather than the page itself. The radius is on the
  top only, since the bottom is off-screen.
- **`s={{ hide: true }}`** rather than a media query. The mobile nav is a
  separate surface, not this one reflowed: a **`Drawer`** from the left,
  holding the same `Nav`, opened by a header button that only shows at `s`
  (`hide s={{ hide: false }}`). Drawer brings the focus trap, scroll lock,
  Escape and focus return a hand-made overlay misses; `flush` keeps its
  `title` for screen readers only. Tie it to the path it was opened on, as
  above, and following a link closes it without an effect.
- **`maxWidth="xl"`** inside the pane. A dashboard is wider than a document;
  `"m"` is for reading.

## 2. Data-driven navigation

```tsx
import { NavGroup, NavItem, selectNavHref } from "@once-ui-system/core";

const current = selectNavHref(pathname, nav.flatMap((i) =>
  i.items ? i.items.map((s) => s.href) : [i.href],
));

<Column fill gap="4" paddingX="8">
  {nav.map((item) =>
    item.items ? (
      <NavGroup
        key={item.key}
        label={item.label}
        icon={item.icon}
        defaultOpen={item.items.some((s) => s.href === current)}>
        {item.items.map((sub) => (
          <NavItem
            key={sub.href}
            href={sub.href}
            label={sub.label}
            badge={sub.badge}
            selected={sub.href === current}
          />
        ))}
      </NavGroup>
    ) : (
      <NavItem
        key={item.href}
        href={item.href}
        icon={item.icon}
        label={item.label}
        selected={item.href === current}
      />
    ),
  )}
</Column>
```

- **`selectNavHref` over `===` or `startsWith`.** An equality check leaves a
  nested route (`/settings/billing/invoices/42`) with nothing highlighted; a
  prefix check lights the parent up alongside its child. It returns the longest
  href that matches, which is the right one.
- **Compute `current` once** for the whole tree, not per item — a child needs to
  know about its siblings to know it is the deepest match.
- **`defaultOpen` from the match**, so the group holding the current page is open
  on arrival.
- Child items take **no icon**. The rail inside `NavGroup` carries the hierarchy;
  a second column of icons competes with it.

## 3. Editor shell

Two panes and a timeline — the shape of a video editor, a page builder, a
diff view. `ai/examples/editor.tsx` (task bundle `editor`) is the whole page
around it: toolbar, layer list, canvas and a working timeline.

```tsx
<Column fill>
  <SplitView
    fill
    leftPanel={<Column fill overflowY="auto">{/* layers, blocks, files */}</Column>}
    rightPanel={<Column fill overflowY="auto">{/* canvas, preview */}</Column>}
    defaultSplit={0.28}
    minSplit={0.2}
    maxSplit={0.6}
    collapseBelow="s"
    labels={{ left: "Layers", right: "Canvas" }}
  />
  <Scrubber
    duration={duration}
    value={time}
    onChange={setTime}
    tracks={tracks}
    onGestureStart={pause}
  />
</Column>
```

- **`overflowY="auto"` on each panel, not on the SplitView.** The divider needs
  the container to stay put while the panes scroll independently.
- **`collapseBelow` + `labels`.** Below the breakpoint the split becomes tabs, and
  `labels` is what they say. Without it the tabs are unlabelled.
- **`onGestureStart` pauses playback.** Scrubbing while playing fights the
  playhead — the drag sets a time, playback immediately moves it.
- **The timeline is a sibling of the split, not inside it.** It spans both panes,
  and putting it in one makes the divider drag it.

## Anti-patterns

- A dashboard with no scrolling pane — the whole document scrolls and the nav
  leaves with it.
- `100vh` in an app shell. Use `100dvh`; `vh` is wrong on mobile the moment the
  browser chrome shows or hides.
- A sticky sidebar without `fitHeight` — it stretches to the row and the sticky
  never engages.
- A mobile menu built from an absolute `Column` and a `zIndex`. Use `Drawer`.
- `pathname === href` or `startsWith` for nav selection. Use `selectNavHref`.
- Icons on both a NavGroup and its children — two columns of icons, no hierarchy.
- `overflow` on the SplitView instead of on its panels — the divider stops
  tracking the pointer.

"use client";

/**
 * Gold example: settings
 * Target: a vertical tab list beside the panel (above it on a phone), a
 * profile form, settings rows with one control each, a group whose
 * sub-settings sit inside it, and a danger zone.
 *
 * The section nav is `Tabs` with `orientation="vertical"`: one `TabPanel` per
 * section, so only the chosen section renders, the list gets the tab roles
 * and arrow keys, and a phone gets the list above the panel from one
 * breakpoint prop. Sections that are routes of their own use `NavItem href`
 * instead. `keepMounted` keeps the profile form's unsaved input when the
 * user looks at another tab.
 *
 * `Setting` is the row — label and description on the left, one control on
 * the right — and stacks into a panel on its own, so a list of them needs no
 * surface around it. `SettingGroup` keeps its sub-settings inside its box,
 * which is what keeps the relationship readable in a long panel.
 */
import {
  Avatar,
  Button,
  Column,
  Form,
  Heading,
  Input,
  NumberInput,
  Row,
  Select,
  Setting,
  SettingGroup,
  Switch,
  Tab,
  TabList,
  TabPanel,
  Tabs,
  Text,
  useToast,
} from "@once-ui-system/core";
import { useState } from "react";

export function SettingsExample() {
  // addToast is stable: call it from handlers and effects directly.
  const { addToast } = useToast();
  const [timezone, setTimezone] = useState("utc");
  const [updates, setUpdates] = useState(true);
  const [digest, setDigest] = useState(true);
  const [digestHour, setDigestHour] = useState(9);

  return (
    <Column as="main" fillWidth horizontal="center" paddingY="48" paddingX="24">
      <Column maxWidth="l" gap="40">
        <Column gap="12">
          <Text variant="label-default-s" onBackground="brand-medium">
            Settings
          </Text>
          <Heading as="h1" variant="display-strong-s">
            Manage your workspace
          </Heading>
        </Column>

        <Tabs defaultValue="profile" orientation="vertical" gap="32" s={{ direction: "column" }}>
          <TabList aria-label="Settings sections" minWidth={14} s={{ direction: "row" }}>
            <Tab value="profile" size="l" prefixIcon="person">
              Profile
            </Tab>
            <Tab value="notifications" size="l" prefixIcon="bell">
              Notifications
            </Tab>
            <Tab value="workspace" size="l" prefixIcon="settings">
              Workspace
            </Tab>
          </TabList>

          <TabPanel value="profile" keepMounted>
            <Column background="surface" border radius="l" padding="24" gap="24">
              <Heading as="h2" variant="heading-strong-m">
                Profile
              </Heading>
              <Row gap="16" vertical="center">
                <Avatar size="l" value="AP" />
                <Column gap="8">
                  <Button size="s" variant="secondary">
                    Upload photo
                  </Button>
                  <Text variant="label-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
                    JPG or PNG, max 2 MB
                  </Text>
                </Column>
              </Row>
              <Form
                as="form"
                columns={{ xl: 2, s: 1 }}
                onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
              >
                <Input id="name" label="Display name" />
                <Input id="email" label="Email" type="email" />
                <Select
                  id="timezone"
                  label="Timezone"
                  value={timezone}
                  onSelect={(value) => setTimezone(value as string)}
                  options={[
                    { value: "utc", label: "UTC" },
                    { value: "cet", label: "Central European Time" },
                    { value: "est", label: "Eastern Time" },
                  ]}
                />
              </Form>
              <Row gap="12">
                <Button onClick={() => addToast({ variant: "success", message: "Profile saved" })}>
                  Save changes
                </Button>
                <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
              </Row>
            </Column>
          </TabPanel>

          <TabPanel value="notifications" gap="8">
            <Heading as="h2" variant="heading-strong-m" paddingBottom="8">
              Notifications
            </Heading>
            <Setting label="Product updates" description="Release notes and changelog">
              <Switch
                checked={updates}
                onToggle={() => setUpdates(!updates)}
                ariaLabel="Product updates"
              />
            </Setting>
            <SettingGroup
              label="Weekly digest"
              info="A summary of the week's activity, sent once."
              control={
                <Switch
                  checked={digest}
                  onToggle={() => setDigest(!digest)}
                  ariaLabel="Weekly digest"
                />
              }
              open={digest}
            >
              <Setting label="Send at" description="Hour of the day, in your timezone">
                <NumberInput
                  id="digest-hour"
                  min={0}
                  max={23}
                  value={digestHour}
                  onChange={setDigestHour}
                />
              </Setting>
            </SettingGroup>
          </TabPanel>

          <TabPanel value="workspace">
            <Column
              background="surface"
              border="danger-alpha-medium"
              radius="l"
              padding="24"
              gap="16"
            >
              <Heading as="h2" variant="heading-strong-m" onBackground="danger-medium">
                Danger zone
              </Heading>
              <Text variant="body-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
                Permanently delete your workspace and all associated data.
              </Text>
              <Row>
                <Button variant="danger" size="s">
                  Delete workspace
                </Button>
              </Row>
            </Column>
          </TabPanel>
        </Tabs>
      </Column>
    </Column>
  );
}
